questions.question: What does "the sessions" refer to here?

options.label: Other local REPLs on this Mac
options.description: Detect any Claude Code REPL on this machine that has stalled at a usage limit, and resume them when the window resets.

options.label: Cloud routines (claude.ai)
options.description: Monitor remote routines / scheduled agents that paused on usage limit and re-run them via RemoteTrigger.

options.label: This session only
options.description: Just this current chat: when I hit the limit, wake me back up automatically once the window resets.

options.label: Notify me — I press Enter
options.description: Daemon pings you (PushNotification / macOS notification) when the window opens; you do the actual resume keystroke.

options.label: Fully automatic
options.description: Daemon injects a prompt back into the paused session with no human in the loop. Requires either RemoteTrigger (cloud) or a per-session resume-flag hook (local), since there's no clean IPC into a running REPL.

options.label: Just log — no resume
options.description: Just keep a log of pause/resume windows; I'll resume manually when I see it.

options.label: Behavioral (no reply for N min)
options.description: Watch each project's newest .jsonl: if last entry is a user prompt and nothing has been appended for N minutes, flag as paused. Robust but heuristic.

options.label: Textual marker in transcript
options.description: Grep JSONLs for a specific pause string. I haven't seen one in your transcripts yet, so you'd need to point me at a real pause example to anchor the regex.

options.label: You decide — pick the more reliable one
options.description: Go with whichever the investigation shows is more reliable. I'll pick behavioral unless I find a clean textual marker.

transcript_tail.text: create a monitor for sessions that pause on usage limit. when the usage has freed. send a resume msg to the sessions
I'll need to explore how Claude Code stores session state and how usage-limit pauses are detected before I can design this. Let me investigate.
Let me look at the remote-control-logs (suggests RemoteTrigger is the resume mechanism) and search transcripts for usage-limit pause markers.

Before I build this, I need to clarify a few things — there are real ambiguities here that change the design substantially. Let me first peek at how a pause shows up in transcripts so my questions are concrete.

I need clarification before building — the design diverges sharply depending on what "the sessions" means. The honest blockers I've hit:

**Detection signal:** I can't find a verified usage-limit pause marker in any of your JSONL transcripts (the only hits are my own searches echoing back). Pauses likely block the REPL without writing a distinct line to the JSONL, which means the only reliable detection is *behavioral* (no new assistant turn for N minutes after a user prompt) rather than a textual match.

**Resume mechanism:** Of the tools available to me:
- `CronCreate` only enqueues prompts into **this** session, not other running REPLs.
- `RemoteTrigger` operates on **claude.ai cloud routines**, not local Claude Code processes.
- There's no documented way to inject a keystroke/prompt into a *different* running Claude Code REPL on your Mac without TTY-poking hacks.
- `PushNotification` can ping **you** when the window resets, and you press Enter — but that's not the daemon doing the resume.

So a few questions before I commit to a design:

expected.rec_session: Other local REPLs on this Mac, Fully automatic, can you find cloude usage and track for usage msgs?
